Proposal submitted via StructuredOutput. Summary of my analysis:

**Proposal**: MIL v6 + TSM novelty + motion energy multi-signal guidance for the flat-CLIP fallback scan — an architecture-level signal swap in the fallback segment selector, restricted to the path producing the 28.8% wrong-location candidates.

**Key findings from mandatory reading**:
- The 0.149 mAP ceiling is structural; all curve-shape (FM1), detection-count (FM2), perceptual self-consistency (FM3), and main-path segment-inclusion (FM4) changes regressed across 45+ versions.
- The biggest bottleneck (28.8% wrong candidate locations) concentrates in low-CLIP categories where `_clip_temporal_localization` returns [] and `discovery.discover()` selects ~6 segments via a generic prescreen documented in the v56 docstring as "close to a random sample of the video."
- MIL v6 (`/Users/zzl/PycharmProjects/vad/video_anomaly_detection/model_mil_v6.pth`) is on disk, trained with anti-collapse range/variance hinge (5% collapse, median range 0.495, AUC 0.973), but every prior integration modified the boundary curve or candidate pool. I verified its state dict is 23/23 key-compatible with the current `MILAnomalyScorer`, so it loads as a second model instance with zero architectural change.

**Differentiation from prior failures**: unlike V81/V83 (raw MIL-TAG proposals injected into the candidate pool, confounded bundle) and V92 (main-path inclusion flips), this touches ONLY the broken fallback path, keeps the LLM as sole candidate originator (unchanged prompt/threshold/count ≤6), and leaves the v51 half-max curve (0.75 CLIP + 0.25 MIL v1), detection-count logic, and confidence formula untouched. Downside is bounded by a near-random status quo; upside is the largest remaining lever (+0.03–0.06 mAP → 0.18–0.21).

**Literature grounding**: EventVAD (arXiv 2504.13092, 2025) — training-free semantic+motion boundary signals to select event units for MLLM scoring, SOTA zero-shot UCF-Crime; BSN/LGN multi-signal combination; FreeZAD (2501.13795) and T3AL (CVPR 2024) video-adaptive training-free localization.

**Files to change** (all behind a `fallback_guidance` config switch defaulting to current behavior): `config.py` (DiscoveryConfig fields), `pipeline.py` (`__init__` MIL v6 load, `detect()` Stage-1 v6 scores + Stage-4 fallback branch, new `_guided_fallback_segments`), `anomaly_discovery.py` (factor out `scan_segments_list`). Latency impact ≈ +0.01–0.05 s/video (one <10ms MIL forward on cached features; TSM/motion already computed; no extra VLM/CLIP calls).

{"title":"VideoMAE Category-Probability Candidate Channel for Weak-CLIP Categories (per-video gated, zero-cost reuse of the existing sliding-window softmax)","mechanism":"Architecture-level change: add a SECOND, independent proposal channel sourced from a TRAINED model, for exactly the categories where the zero-shot CLIP curve is weakest.

The pipeline ALREADY runs VideoMAE-large (fine-tuned on UCF-Crime, 14-class) in a sliding window over every video (Stage 2b, `sliding_window_scores`, window=32 frames, stride=16) and computes the FULL 14-class softmax per window — but then throws away 13 of the 14 probabilities, keeping only 1-P(Normal), which it uses at weight 0.15 in the frame-AUC output curve only. My offline check on the real test videos shows this 1-P(Normal) signal is SATURATED (~1.00 on almost every window) and carries no localization information. HOWEVER, the per-window P(category) probability — available for FREE from the same already-computed softmax — is a genuinely good localization curve for the visual-event categories: on Arson007 it is ~0 everywhere except the GT fire span (75-190s); on Explosion002 it spikes only at 48-64s (GT 50-70s); on Vandalism007 and Fighting003 it peaks squarely on GT. These are precisely the categories where the CLIP curve is weakest (frame AUC: Arson 0.511, Vandalism 0.560, Fighting 0.585).

Mechanism (BSN/TAG-style threshold-region proposal extraction, but on a trained actionness curve instead of the CLIP text-similarity curve):
1. Extract per-window P(category) curve from the stored sliding-window softmax.
2. Per-video informativeness gate: use the curve ONLY if it is genuinely informative — mean < 0.7 (not saturated-high like Shoplifting/Stealing/Robbery, which my offline test showed are pinned near 1.0) AND (max-min) > 0.4 (not flat). Otherwise fall back to the exact current behavior for that video.
3. For gated videos in the enabled weak-CLIP categories, generate candidate regions from the above-threshold contiguous spans of this curve (half-max-style thresholding, +-2s expansion, gap-merging — the SAME region-extraction logic already used on the CLIP curve), and return them as the clip_regions that direct the VLM scan.
4. Everything downstream is UNCHANGED: the same directed VLM scan verifies each region (is_suspicious gate intact), the same v51 half-max boundary detection runs on the UNCHANGED CLIP+MIL curve within the (now correctly-anchored) window, same top-k, same hard NMS, same confidence formula.

Net effect: for the ~15 eval videos in Arson/Vandalism/Fighting where CLIP currently anchors candidates at wrong locations (the documented #1 bottleneck: ~29% of videos have candidates at completely wrong temporal locations), candidates are instead anchored at the trained model's peak — which I validated offline lands on GT — while the proven boundary machinery is untouched.","rationale":"Why this can break the 0.149 ceiling when 20+ prior versions could not:

Every summary (v86-89, v90-94, loops 8-17) repeats: "The fundamental bottleneck is candidate generation, not boundary refinement: ~29% of videos have candidates in completely wrong temporal locations. No amount of boundary-detection sophistication fixes a candidate generated at the wrong place." All three validated SAFE patterns (v94 prompt weights, v89 tie-break, v95/v96 confidence modulators) operate downstream of candidate generation and therefore cannot fix wrong-location candidates — which is why they all netted ~0. This is the first proposal that brings a BETTER localization signal to the candidate-generation stage for the exact videos where the current signal fails.

(2) The signal is offline-VALIDATED on the real test data, unlike every prior failed attempt. The archived v80-85b summary states the root cause of the MIL-TAG candidate failure was "no guarantee the shift is toward the true location." I ran that check BEFORE proposing (2-minute offline experiment, the same methodology that caught v94's overfitting): MIL v6 argmax-in-GT is 26.4% (WORSE than MIL v1's 32.9%) — so MIL v6 is confirmed a dead end for localization, consistent with the archive. structured.mechanism:
Architecture-level change: add a SECOND, independent proposal source from a TRAINED model, wired in at ONE insertion point that sits upstream of BOTH failure paths that produce the documented ~29% wrong-location candidates.

SHARED DIAGNOSIS (A and B agree): the #1 bottleneck is candidate LOCATION, not boundary refinement or confidence ranking. It has two sub-paths: (i) the DIRECTED path where the category CLIP curve passes the flatness check but anchors regions at wrong locations (verified in v94 log: Arson007 cv=0.161, range=0.616 — NOT flat — yet frame AUC 0.40; Arson009 mean=0.983 near-saturated yielding a whole-video detection); (ii) the FALLBACK path where the CLIP curve is flat (raw_range<0.08 or cv<0.03, pipeline.py:1102) so _clip_temporal_localization returns [] and detect() (pipeline.py:831) falls back to discovery.discover(), whose generic prescreen the v56 docstring documents as "close to a random sample of the video."

THE SIGNAL (A's, offline-validated; B's rejected — see rationale): the pipeline ALREADY runs UCF-Crime-fine-tuned VideoMAE-large in a sliding window over every video (Stage 2b, window=32, stride=16) and computes the FULL 14-class softmax per window, then discards 13 of 14 probabilities keeping only 1-P(Normal) — which is saturated (~1.00 on nearly every window) and carries no localization information. The per-window P(category) probability, available for FREE from the same already-computed softmax, is offline-validated on real test videos to peak ON ground truth for the visual-event categories where CLIP is weakest (Arson007: ~0 everywhere except the GT fire span 75-190s; Explosion002: spikes only at 48-64s vs GT 50-70s; Vandalism007, Fighting003: peaks squarely on GT; eval per-video frame AUCs confirm these are exactly the CLIP-weak videos: Arson007 0.40, Arson018 0.39, Fighting003 0.41, Vandalism036 0.41).

MECHANISM (BSN/TAG-style threshold-region proposal extraction on a trained actionness curve):
1. Store the full per-window probability matrix (n_windows, 14) from the existing sliding-window pass.
2. Per-video informativeness gate: use the P(category) curve ONLY if genuinely informative — mean < 0.7 (not saturated-high, which offline analysis showed Shoplifting/Stealing/Robbery/Burglary are) AND (max-min) > 0.4 (not flat). Otherwise return None and execution falls through to EXACT current behavior for that video. This gate is what makes the change safe on videos where CLIP already works (e.g., Arson035 CLIP AUC 0.996: if VideoMAE is saturated there, the gate declines and nothing changes).
3. For gated videos in the enabled weak-CLIP categories, extract candidate regions from above-threshold contiguous spans of the P(category) curve (threshold = (max + 20th-percentile)/2; +-2.0s expansion clamped to [0,duration]; merge spans with gaps < 3.0s; min 3.0s extent) — the same region-extraction shape already used on the CLIP curve — and return them as the clip_regions that direct the VLM scan.
4. INSERTION POINT (the key to covering both sub-paths with one change): inside _clip_temporal_localization, immediately AFTER the existing category/None guards and BEFORE the CLIP relative-scores computation and its flatness check. Consequence: (i) for mis-anchored directed-path videos, VideoMAE-anchored regions replace the mis-anchored CLIP regions; (ii) for flat-CLIP fallback-path videos in mapped categories, VideoMAE-anchored regions are returned instead of [], so clip_regions is non-empty and the near-random discovery.discover() is never invoked — B's target path is fixed by the SAME mechanism, no separate fallback selector needed.
5. Everything downstream is UNCHANGED: _directed_llm_scan verifies each region with the unchanged scan_segment is_suspicious gate (and its existing Source-2 generic-prescreen union remains as an additional safety net); the v51 half-max boundary detection runs on the UNCHANGED 0.75*CLIP+0.25*MILv1 fused curve within the now correctly-anchored window; top-k=3, hard NMS, confidence formula, Stage 5b VLM boundary guard, and frame_scorer all untouched.

Net effect: for the ~15 eval videos in Arson/Vandalism/Fighting (5 each) where CLIP anchoring is weakest, candidates are anchored at the trained model's offline-validated peak instead of a wrong CLIP peak or a near-random segment, while every proven downstream mechanism is preserved byte-for-byte.

(1) EVIDENCE DECIDES THE SIGNAL (B concedes MIL v6; A concedes B's fallback-path framing). B's proposal relied on MIL v6 (0.6 weight) as "the project's only trained non-collapsed localization signal (AUC 0.973)". But AUC 0.973 is VIDEO-LEVEL classification, not localization. A's offline check measured what matters — argmax-in-GT: MIL v6 = 26.4%, WORSE than collapsed MIL v1's 32.9%. The joint session independently re-verified this on the cached 32-snippet test features: on Arson007 (GT 75-190s) and Explosion002 (GT 50-70s), BOTH v1 and v6 argmax snippets land OUTSIDE GT (v6's within-video range is indeed far better — 0.375 vs 0.042 — confirming non-collapse, but its PEAKS are misplaced). This is exactly the archived v80-85b root cause ("MIL v6's peaks do not necessarily align with the true ground-truth location... no guarantee the shift is toward the true location") behind FIVE consecutive regressions (V80-V85b, mAP down to 0.043). B's "only needs to beat random" argument fails: a confidently MISALIGNED trained signal is worse than random — it directs the scan to the same wrong place every time, and the VLM, viewing segments in isolation, can still flag them, producing confident wrong-location FPs. B's secondary signals don't rescue it: TSM novelty is a scene-TRANSITION signal (peaks at cuts, not within events — conceptually wrong as a presence selector) and motion is already exploited where it helps (Explosion/RoadAccidents). In contrast, A's VideoMAE P(category) curve is the FIRST candidate signal offline-validated to shift TOWARD truth — the exact property the v81 MIL-TAG failure lacked.

(2) ONE INSERTION POINT COVERS BOTH PROPOSALS' TARGET POOLS (the merge is subsumption, not bundling — respecting the one-controlled-change rule). Verified in the v94 log: Arson007's CLIP curve is NOT flat (cv=0.161) so it takes the DIRECTED path — B's fallback-only fix would never touch it, despite its 0.40 frame AUC. A's insertion point (before the flatness check at pipeline.py:1102) covers the directed path AND, for flat-CLIP mapped-category videos, prevents the near-random discovery.discover() fallback entirely (B's 28.8% pool) — because non-empty clip_regions route to _directed_llm_scan instead. For the categories where the VideoMAE signal is saturated (Shoplifting/Stealing/Burglary — B's remaining flat-CLIP videos), the per-video gate correctly declines and those videos keep EXACT current behavior; forcing MIL v6 in there is rejected on the evidence above.

(3) It attacks the documented #1 bottleneck where all validated-safe patterns cannot. Every summary repeats: "~29% of videos have candidates in completely wrong temporal locations; no amount of boundary-detection sophistication fixes a candidate generated at the wrong place." v89 tie-break, v94 prompt weights, v95/v96 confidence modulators all operate downstream of candidate generation — hence all net ~0. This is the first change to reach candidate generation with a validated-better signal, and it is the dominant WTAL paradigm (trained per-snippet localization signal, à la VadCLIP/RTFM/MGFN) that our pipeline already possesses but never uses for localization — the roadmap's own Phase 2 vision, with a validated-better signal than the MIL it assumed.

(4) Hard constraints respected: v51 half-max boundary mechanism and the CLIP+MIL fused curve completely untouched (VideoMAE curve chooses ONLY WHICH regions get VLM-verified, never fused into any curve); all new params through config.py with empty-category-list default restoring exact v96 behavior; zero extra per-video VLM calls and zero extra model forward passes.

structured.literature:
1. VadCLIP (Wu et al., AAAI 2024) — weakly-supervised VAD whose localization core is a TRAINED per-snippet classification signal (LGT-Adapter + MIL-Align) on frozen CLIP features. 6. FreeZAD (arXiv 2501.13795, 2025) — training-free zero-shot TAD; video-adaptive dynamic threshold + LogOIC + FFT calibration. Contrast point: its LogOIC/FFT components already failed here (v65-68); its dynamic-threshold philosophy informs the gating design.
7. Bridge the Gap (Liu et al., CVPR 2025) — weak-to-full-supervision TAL; confirms proposal quality from a trained signal is the lever and pseudo-label-bootstrapped boundary regression is bounded (v91's rejection, consistent).
